overview.title: Overview
overview.lead: Aether brings activity from all your tools together, so you can see the people, AI agents, connections, and results behind it — and trust the answer, because every step is recorded.

blocks.title: New here?
blocks.x: Pick your role in the For your role tab for a guided path.

Aether collects activity from your websites, apps, and connected tools. It cleans that activity up, matches it to the right people and companies, and shows how everything connects — through the product, developer tools, and intelligence views.

items.title: See one customer across systems
items.x: A Profile joins web, CRM, commerce, and payments evidence into one explainable view.

items.title: Follow the path to revenue
items.x: Journeys show how far people got, where they dropped off, and what moved them.

items.title: Ask one question across everyone
items.x: Lenses project a dimension — value, risk, attribution — across every entity.

items.title: Know what is uncertain
items.x: Evidence, inference, approval, and outcome stay separate states.

governance.title: Governance and security
governance.lead: How tenant scope, consent, credentials, and human authority are enforced.

items.title: Data separation
items.x: Every event, record, connection, and key belongs to one customer. No part of Aether returns another customer’s data.

items.title: Consent gating
items.x: Each event type maps to a required purpose via `EVENT_CONSENT_PURPOSE`. Batches declare consent.

items.title: No secrets in browsers
items.x: Tenant and app IDs are identifiers. Server keys stay server-side.

items.title: Human authority
items.x: Requested, authorized, executed, verified, and measured are separate states.

blocks.x: Narrower scopes exist for subsystems, such as `commerce:read` or `agent:manage`.

blocks.title: Identity never runs ahead of consent
blocks.x: Device fingerprinting is gated on the `personalization` purpose and never runs while Do Not Track is honored.

signals.title: Signals
signals.lead: A signal is one thing that happened — a page viewed, an order placed, an agent running a tool. Aether checks it, adds context, and files it in the right place.

blocks.x: Every signal carries a `type` from one registry shared by every SDK and the backend — a little over 400 types across about two dozen families. Unknown types are dropped at the SDK with a debug warning, never mislabeled.

journeys.title: Journeys
journeys.lead: A journey is the path someone takes through your product — signing up, checking out, an agent-assisted task — step by step.

blocks.x: A signal is one event. A journey groups many under one lifecycle, so you can ask how far people got and where they dropped off.

items.title: Automatic pause
items.x: Hidden tabs pause the journey. After `journeyTimeoutMs` (default 30 min) it is abandoned, not silently continued.

items.title: Cross-device
items.x: When identity resolves, the journey resumes on the new device as one continuous path.

items.title: SPA routes
items.x: Route changes during an active journey become checkpoints automatically.

lenses.title: Lenses
lenses.lead: A lens is a way of looking at the same data from a different angle. It never changes or copies your data — only what stands out.

blocks.title: 360s vs. lenses
blocks.x: A 360 answers “tell me everything about this entity.” A lens answers “show me this dimension across entities.”
Every lens set has one base lens, `standard`, plus zero or more overlays. Composition is order-stable: `temporal` then `campaign` equals `campaign` then `temporal`.

head: Overlay
Foregrounds
rows: Connections and how many steps away they are

blocks.x: The Explore page (`/explore`) shows the lens dock for the focused object. Each lens shows its real state — available, not entitled, no access, or not ready — instead of being hidden.

imports.title: Imports
imports.lead: Upload a file, match its columns to Aether, check it, approve it, and commit — with the option to roll it back.

blocks.x: `entity`, `identifier`, `action`, `relationship`, `resource`, `evidence`, `metric`, `governance_fact`, and `unmapped_record`. A row that maps to nothing is kept as `unmapped_record`, never dropped.

items.title: Analyze
items.x: Each column gets an inferred type and a sensitivity: pii, identifier, secret, governance, or none.

items.title: Governance gate
items.x: Sensitive mappings move to `review_required`. Approval needs admin and a passing validation.

items.title: Replay and rollback
items.x: Rollback revokes the commit’s edges and deletes its Bronze rows. The source file is kept for replay.

blocks.title: Limits
blocks.x: XLSX, Parquet, and archives are rejected. Files are capped at 32 MB. The upload wizard UI is a follow-on.

items.q: What happens to rows that do not map?
items.a: They are kept as `unmapped_record`, never dropped, so you can remap and replay.
Yes. Rollback removes the connections it created and deletes its raw rows.

why-aether.title: Why Aether
why-aether.lead: Work no longer runs only through people. It runs through people, AI agents, and software working together. The organizations that can see how those pieces connect will do best.

blocks.x: Organizations operate with fragmented data, fragmented identities, fragmented attribution, and fragmented awareness. As people and agents interact across more systems, that fragmentation gets expensive: visibility, leverage, and adaptability are lost.

items.title: Relationships are the unit
items.x: Records matter because of how they relate over time, not only because they exist.

items.title: Agents are participants
items.x: Agents act for people and with each other. Their relationships belong in the same graph.

items.title: Governance is part of the product
items.x: Consent, policy, explainability, and human authority apply to everything.

blocks.x: The manual stitching of analytics platforms, attribution tooling, identity systems, relationship analysis, fraud intelligence, and disconnected event pipelines. Aether sits between existing layers as connective infrastructure — it does not ask you to rip them out.

head: Aether is
Aether is not

items: Do Not Track is honored; fingerprinting never runs while it is on.

items.q: Can I get my data out?
items.a: Yes, through governed exports under `/v1/data-exchange/exports`, and audit exports under `/v1/audit/exports`.

items.q: Does Aether take actions on its own?
items.a: Not consequential ones. Critical actions above set thresholds need a person’s approval.
Multi-tenant cloud by default. Enterprise isolated, sovereign, on-premise, and air-gapped are supported models.
